diagrams.title: Earn the Commission Through Five Controlled Handoffs
diagrams.subtitle: Exclusive authority, verified counterparties, and documented settlement.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Applies to specialist asset and private-company transactions after jurisdiction and license review. Annual revenue means retained transaction commissions, never underlying asset value, buyer deposits, or escrow principal. First-deal timing is 3–12 months; the workflow is not a one-month closing forecast.
diagrams.caption: Each handoff requires a named owner and a complete evidence packet. Automation moves records and reminders; accountable people verify authority, representations, and closing conditions.

stages.label: Classify and mandate
stages.value: Execute scoped exclusive authority before marketing the asset.
stages.detail: The principal confirms transaction form, operating jurisdictions, license requirements, seller authority, commission basis, exclusivity, excluded buyers, and tail provisions. Reject unsupported ownership claims before signing an engagement.

stages.label: Build the evidence room
stages.value: Reconcile seller claims against indexed supporting records.
stages.detail: The document contractor assembles ownership records, operating statements, material contracts, asset lists, and lien information in SharePoint. Restrict access by role and record every material correction.

stages.label: Match and qualify
stages.value: Introduce authorized buyers with verified capacity and fit.
stages.detail: Use HubSpot sector tags and Airtable buyer criteria to shortlist counterparties. Confirm decision authority, funding evidence, acquisition criteria, and confidentiality terms before releasing sensitive seller materials.

stages.label: Negotiate and diligence
stages.value: Track signed terms, exceptions, and unresolved closing conditions.
stages.detail: The principal leads commercial negotiations while independent counsel handles transaction documents. Track LOI terms, diligence exceptions, lender dependencies, secured-party releases, and deadlines in a milestone register.

stages.label: Settle and reconcile
stages.value: Release the earned commission through documented settlement instructions.
stages.detail: An independent escrow provider handles transaction funds. Verify changed payment instructions through a known telephone contact, reconcile the closing statement, and record only the operator's retained commission.

diagrams.title: Ten Closings From One Tracked Annual Cohort
diagrams.subtitle: A mature pipeline illustration supporting $550,000 in retained commissions.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The five stages are nested counts from the same 200-owner cohort, observed across its complete sales cycle. They are planning assumptions, not measured conversion benchmarks. Ten completed transactions at $55,000 retained commission each produce the canonical $550,000 Base-Case annual revenue. A steady-state annual pipeline can contain overlapping cohorts.
diagrams.caption: Stage conversions are 50%, 40%, 50%, and 50%; overall owner-to-close conversion is 5%. Deduplicate seller mandates rather than counting multiple buyer conversations as separate deals.

stages.label: Relevant owner accounts
stages.value: 200 screened owners with a documented transaction thesis.
stages.detail: Research owners inside one specialist sector and record a plausible sale trigger, asset profile, decision-maker, and permitted contact channel. Purchased contact volume alone does not qualify an account.

stages.label: Qualified seller discussions
stages.value: 100 owners confirm authority, motivation, timing, and fit.
stages.detail: Fifty percent of the screened cohort completes a substantive discussion. Capture valuation expectations, records availability, ownership structure, and willingness to disclose defects before offering representation.

stages.label: Executed exclusive mandates
stages.value: 40 sellers execute scoped mandates with workable fee terms.
stages.detail: Forty percent of qualified discussions becomes an exclusive engagement. Record fee triggers, buyer exclusions, conflicts, termination rights, and tail dates; an unsigned proposal remains outside the mandate count.

stages.label: Signed transaction LOIs
stages.value: 20 mandated sellers reach documented preliminary transaction terms.
stages.detail: Half the executed mandates reaches a signed LOI with a qualified buyer. Count each seller mandate once, even if a replacement buyer later signs another LOI after the first transaction fails.

stages.label: Completed commission events
stages.value: 10 closings earn $55,000 each in retained commissions.
stages.detail: Half the LOI-stage mandates closes. An illustrative $1,100,000 asset price at a 5% retained commission produces $55,000; the resulting $11,000,000 aggregate asset value is excluded from operator revenue.

diagrams.title: $550,000 Revenue to $206,250 Owner Net
diagrams.subtitle: Four expense deductions reconcile exactly to the 37.5% Base-Case margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: USD annually. Opening revenue and closing profit are absolute total bars; the four intervening bars are signed deductions. The expense allocation is editorial, while scenario totals are canonical. Conservative: $100,000 revenue, 25% margin, $25,000 owner net, 1 FT + 3 C. Base: $550,000 revenue, 37.5% margin, $206,250 owner net, 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled: $1,000,000 revenue, 50% margin, $500,000 owner net, 2 FT + 4 C.
diagrams.caption: $550,000 - $150,000 - $108,000 - $60,000 - $25,750 = $206,250. Total expenses are $343,750, or 62.5% of retained commissions. Owner net is modeled before personal income taxes; owner draws are not a second expense.

stages.label: Retained commission revenue
stages.value: $550,000 earned from ten completed commission events.
stages.detail: Opening total equals ten closings multiplied by $55,000 retained commission. Outside-broker shares are excluded before this revenue basis is measured; escrow principal and asset purchase prices never enter it.

stages.label: Deal-specific delivery costs
stages.value: Deduct $150,000 for externally purchased transaction support.
stages.detail: Budget $15,000 per closing-equivalent for specialist inspection, transaction support, travel, and diligence. The annual allocation includes work on failed deals. Vendors are purchased services, not additional pod seats.

stages.label: Three contractor seats
stages.value: Deduct $108,000 across three defined contractor scopes.
stages.detail: Allocate $36,000 annually to each core contractor scope: research, documents, and transaction coordination. These are budgeted service scopes rather than three full-time employee salaries; classification follows actual work arrangements.

stages.label: Core operating overhead
stages.value: Deduct $60,000 for systems, prospecting, and administration.
stages.detail: Allocate $5,000 monthly to CRM, secure document storage, sector data, prospecting, bookkeeping, and administration. Combined with $9,000 monthly contractor spend, recurring modeled overhead is $14,000 monthly.

stages.label: Insurance and dispute expense
stages.value: Deduct $25,750 for coverage and modeled dispute costs.
stages.detail: Include transaction-services coverage, deductibles, and dispute-resolution costs as annual modeled expenses. This line is not an escrow balance or a cash reserve transfer. Avoid duplicating deal-specific delivery costs.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.value: $206,250 remains after all four modeled expense categories.
stages.detail: Closing total equals $550,000 multiplied by 37.5%. The full-time principal receives the residual owner economics; no separate principal salary is deducted in this illustrative owner-operated expense bridge.

diagrams.title: Compare Retained Fees, Not Asset Prices
diagrams.subtitle: Five independent commission illustrations per $1,000,000 of closed asset value.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric bars show retained commission dollars on a common $1,000,000 underlying transaction denominator. Rates are negotiated planning assumptions, not published market averages or promised yields. Bars are alternatives, not components of the Base-Case revenue model. All examples assume no outside-broker share and no separately modeled settlement charge.
diagrams.caption: Choose a niche using accessible mandates, required licenses, diligence workload, and closing probability. A higher fee rate can still produce weaker annual economics if transactions stall.

stages.label: Operating-business asset sale
stages.value: $50,000 retained at an illustrative five-percent fee.
stages.detail: A negotiated 5% commission on a $1,000,000 asset sale yields $50,000. Validate business-opportunity licensing where applicable; use independent escrow and resolve purchase-price allocation before settlement.

stages.label: Private-company control sale
stages.value: $30,000 retained at an illustrative three-percent fee.
stages.detail: A negotiated 3% commission on a $1,000,000 control transaction yields $30,000. Document securities registration or exemption analysis, buyer control, active management, and settlement without broker custody.

stages.label: Industrial real property
stages.value: $25,000 retained at an illustrative two-and-a-half-percent fee.
stages.detail: A negotiated 2.5% commission on a $1,000,000 property sale yields $25,000. Perform brokerage through the required licensed structure and route proceeds through the designated title or escrow closing provider.

stages.label: Specialist production equipment
stages.value: $20,000 retained at an illustrative two-percent fee.
stages.detail: A negotiated 2% commission on a $1,000,000 equipment package yields $20,000. Match serial numbers to inspection reports, search applicable lien records, and obtain secured-party releases tied to settlement.

stages.label: Commercial aircraft asset
stages.value: $15,000 retained at an illustrative one-and-a-half-percent fee.
stages.detail: A negotiated 1.5% commission on a $1,000,000 aircraft sale yields $15,000. Use aviation-specific title and escrow expertise, verify recorded interests and maintenance records, and resolve applicable registration requirements.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before a Mandate Becomes Executable
diagrams.subtitle: Each unresolved branch returns the transaction for correction or rejection.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Stage numbers identify sequential decision nodes, not risk scores. At each node, a documented pass advances to the next check; an unresolved result stops the affected activity. Apply current law to the transaction's actual jurisdictions and structure. An NCNDA cannot substitute for a required license.
diagrams.caption: Record the evidence, reviewer, date, and resulting action for every node. Recheck after a switch from an asset sale to an equity sale, a new buyer, or changed payment instructions.

stages.label: Asset and license classification
stages.value: Proceed only after identifying the asset and required authority.
stages.detail: Identify asset versus securities transfers and every relevant jurisdiction. California BPC 10130 and 10131 cover specified real-property and business-opportunity brokerage activities. If required authority is absent, stop brokerage activity until an appropriate structure exists.

stages.label: Securities route and exclusions
stages.value: Proceed only with a documented registration or exemption route.
stages.detail: For securities transactions, test 15 U.S.C. 78o(b)(13), including current eligible-company limits, buyer control, active management, prohibited activities, and disqualifications. Required dual-representation disclosure and written consent must be documented. An asset-only conclusion requires its own recorded basis.

stages.label: Authority, claims, and title
stages.value: Proceed only with supported representations and releasable interests.
stages.detail: Verify signatory authority, agency disclosures, conflicts, and evidence behind material claims. For securities, 17 CFR 240.10b-5 addresses deceptive statements and omissions. For secured assets, apply enacted UCC 9-315 and 9-513. Scope NCNDA introductions, exclusions, duration, and remedies without treating the document as automatic protection.

stages.label: Funds and release instructions
stages.value: Proceed only through verified settlement and permitted funds handling.
stages.detail: Use independent escrow and known-contact callbacks for payment changes. The M&A exemption under 15 U.S.C. 78o(b)(13) excludes specified custody activities. California BPC 10145 governs covered broker trust-money handling. If release instructions conflict, freeze disbursement and obtain corrected instructions.

diagrams.title: One Principal, Three Bounded Contractor Scopes
diagrams.subtitle: The Base pod has four people; the Scaled pod expands to six.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each stage represents one core person: 1 FT + 3 C. Conservative and Base retain this four-person structure; Scaled uses 2 FT + 4 C by adding one full-time execution lead and one contractor for buyer research. Contractor status depends on actual working conditions and applicable law.
diagrams.caption: The principal owns mandates, negotiations, and commercial decisions. Automation handles matching suggestions, milestone alerts, and document completeness checks, never substantive verification or unattended movement of client funds.

stages.label: Principal and mandate owner
stages.value: One full-time operator owns representation and commercial decisions.
stages.detail: Qualify sellers, confirm the permitted brokerage scope, sign engagements, negotiate commercial terms, and resolve conflicts. Maintain the cash forecast and capacity plan. Scaled adds a full-time execution lead rather than silently overloading this seat.

stages.label: Buyer and seller researcher
stages.value: One contractor maintains evidence-backed prospect and buyer records.
stages.detail: Maintain HubSpot records, Airtable matching criteria, ownership research, buyer capacity evidence, and suppression lists. The Base allocation is $36,000 annually for the defined scope. Scaled adds another research contractor to increase qualified coverage.

stages.label: Document and diligence coordinator
stages.value: One contractor keeps the evidence room complete and controlled.
stages.detail: Maintain SharePoint permissions, document indexes, version history, request lists, and discrepancy logs. Escalate contradictory seller statements rather than editing them into consistency. The Base allocation is $36,000 annually for this service scope.

stages.label: Transaction milestone coordinator
stages.value: One contractor tracks dependencies through independent escrow settlement.
stages.detail: Maintain deadlines, counsel requests, inspection dependencies, secured-party releases, and closing checklists. Prepare reconciliations without controlling client funds. The Base allocation is $36,000 annually; counsel and escrow providers remain external vendors.

diagrams.title: A $60,000 Launch Budget Inside the Canonical Range
diagrams.subtitle: Four distinct buckets within the $15,000–$100,000 USD startup envelope.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are USD capital allocations totaling $60,000; they are not four expense deductions from the annual scorecard. The startup range is $15,000–$100,000, monthly operating expense range is $3,000–$18,000, and first-deal timing is 3–12 months. Cash reserved for runway is not itself an expense.
diagrams.caption: $12,000 + $8,000 + $15,000 + $25,000 = $60,000. The $25,000 runway bucket covers about 8.3 months at $3,000 monthly, but only 1.8 months at the modeled $14,000 Base recurring burn. Do not deploy Base spending before the cash plan can support delayed closings.

stages.label: Authority and engagement setup
stages.value: $12,000 establishes the scoped operating and contracting structure.
stages.detail: Fund jurisdiction-specific license analysis, required applications, engagement drafting, agency disclosures, insurance setup, and escrow-provider onboarding. Confirm actual requirements before allocating money to promotion for a service the operator cannot yet perform.

stages.label: Data room and operating systems
stages.value: $8,000 establishes secure records and repeatable transaction workflows.
stages.detail: Configure HubSpot, Airtable, SharePoint, access controls, backup procedures, templates, and electronic signatures. Separate initial setup from recurring subscriptions; each paid invoice belongs once in the cash ledger and receives appropriate accounting treatment.

stages.label: Sector research and mandate acquisition
stages.value: $15,000 funds a bounded specialist-market acquisition program.
stages.detail: Purchase targeted sector data, conduct owner research, prepare evidence-led outreach, and attend selected industry meetings. Release spend in measured batches based on qualified discussions and signed mandates rather than raw contact counts.

stages.label: Uncommitted operating runway
stages.value: $25,000 remains available for lean operations and closing delays.
stages.detail: Keep this bucket liquid and separate from client funds. Twelve months at the $3,000 monthly floor requires $36,000 before additional deal costs; this allocation therefore requires lower deployment, added capital, or an explicit pause plan for a prolonged delay.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to a Documented Brokerage Operating System
diagrams.subtitle: Build executable mandates and pipeline evidence, not an invented first-month close.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are cumulative milestone days: 7, 14, 21, and 30. Work begins only within an authorized service scope. Licensing, seller readiness, and diligence can extend the schedule. The canonical first-deal window remains 3–12 months; these milestones do not forecast commission receipts.
diagrams.caption: End the sprint with an auditable mandate process, qualified counterparty records, a tested document workflow, and a cash plan that survives missed closing dates.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Define the niche, permitted activities, and cash constraints.
stages.detail: Select one asset category and operating jurisdiction; document license and securities analysis, excluded activities, escrow arrangements, and a 13-week cash forecast. Complete the four statutory and risk checks before launching brokerage outreach.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Install the mandate packet and controlled evidence workflow.
stages.detail: Prepare the exclusive engagement, scoped NCNDA, agency disclosures, seller questionnaire, buyer qualification checklist, and document index. Configure HubSpot stages and SharePoint access, then test a sample record without real client funds.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Run a bounded owner-research and buyer-matching pilot.
stages.detail: Research 25 relevant owners and 15 plausible buyers as activity targets, not conversion promises. Log authority, sector fit, acquisition criteria, contact permissions, and evidence gaps. Review qualified conversations before expanding outreach spend.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Audit the pilot and rehearse a failed-closing response.
stages.detail: Review actual mandate progress, reconcile the cash ledger, and test document retrieval, milestone alerts, payment-change callbacks, and a canceled transaction. Assign remediation owners and revise the next 30-day work plan using observed conversion evidence.
